messages.author: 28c4bdfcd7324d44
messages.subject: Mean specification in an ar1 process
parts:
Hello,

I'd like to ask a "weird" question, if possible:

suppose that we've got two random processes -- both autoregressive of order one -- each with very small variance whose random path we wish to estimate.
Is it possible that we could -- somehow -- initialize their starting values (that could be drawn, par example, via a simple GLM) in order to "help" the identifiability process?

Thanks in advance,
Maria

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mean specification in an ar1 process
parts:
On Sun, 2015-06-14 at 12:36 -0700, Maria Skoularidou wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'd like to ask a "weird" question, if possible:
>
> suppose that we've got two random processes -- both autoregressive of
> order one -- each with very small variance whose random path we wish
> to estimate.
> Is it possible that we could -- somehow -- initialize their starting
> values (that could be drawn, par example, via a simple GLM) in order
> to "help" the identifiability process?

you can initialise the hyperparameters, like the marginal precision and
correlation in the case of the AR(1) process, but the AR1 process
itself, is initialised to zero.

for the hyperparameters, use the keywork initial, like

hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(prec)))

and similar for the correction, and recall to give the initial value in
the internal parametermerisation.

Best
H
